$comment: Every example of contract/examples with the schema it is validated against, whether it must pass, the rule it illustrates and why. An invalid example violates exactly one constraint; violation states the failure check-contract.py must report (kind parse, schema or semantic; check is the JSON Schema keyword or the semantic check id; path is a JSON pointer into the example) and no other failure may occur.

examples.reason: A complete list: the task fields agents ask for, has_more false, the filter computed in the tool and echoed in scope, titles declared untrusted once.
A first page: has_more true with exactly one continuation (next_cursor).
External text (an injected instruction in the description) is declared in meta.untrusted; it is data, never instructions (SEC-002).
An update notice read from the local cache rides on an ordinary read in meta.notices.
The blueprint's not-found envelope: exact error keys, dispatch_state and next_action; a read that gets a 404 is not_started.
An unknown command names the problem, the closest full path, the usage line and the sibling commands.
A measured first guess (--all, from the fleet guess list) answered with an exact did_you_mean and the next step.
An unsupported format is E_USAGE unsupported_format, emitted as JSON.
A connection failure before sending: E_NETWORK, retryable, dispatch_state not_started.
HTTP 429 maps to E_RATE_LIMITED with retry_after_ms; on a read the error is not_started.
Upstream text goes in details.upstream_message and is listed in meta.untrusted; message stays the tool's own sentence.
An ambiguous name returns E_AMBIGUOUS (exit 2) with candidate refs.
E_HUMAN_REQUIRED (exit 9) says what the person must do and what to run afterwards; the refused read is not_started.
A declared extension code (archery-cli's E_2FA_REQUIRED, exit 9): the name may start with a digit after E_, and its details carry dispatch_state and next_action like every error.
mr update --dry-run: the preview, a canonical token bound to the operation id, its expiry (15 minutes) and the operation id.
A write called without --dry-run or --confirm: the refusal carries the same preview, token, expiry and operation id as a dry-run.
A dangerous command without --dangerous is refused before the preview with problem dangerous_flag_required.
A dry-run that cannot apply: ok true with blocked_by, and confirm_token and expires_at null.
A confirmed write: the receipt with every outcome dimension and the read-back of the changed fields; ok follows receipt_rules (rule 9).
Base profile: change applied with verification not_run is still ok true.
The same idempotency key with the same request returns the original receipt with replayed true.
A reply lost after sending: E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN (exit 6, not retryable) with operation_id and lookup; receipt rule 1.
GitLab ignored an assignee who is not a member; the read-back disagrees, so receipt rule 7 gives E_VERIFY_FAILED.
Part of a single write took effect: receipt rule 2 gives E_PARTIAL.
The upstream refused the write and nothing changed: receipt rule 4 gives the apply step's cause code.
A delivery the destination refused: receipt rule 6 gives E_FORBIDDEN.
GitLab created the variable unmasked, so the tool deleted it again: change rolled_back, and receipt rule 5 gives the cause, E_VERIFY_FAILED.
A confirm with changed inputs is token_mismatch naming the first differing parameter; nothing is sent.
A repeated create whose earlier operation was resolved by hand as applied is refused with idempotency_resolved, naming that operation, and nothing is sent.
While an unknown outcome is unresolved, new writes to the same target are E_CONFLICT unresolved_operation.
A write refused locally for lack of scope: details.scope says why, where and what to grant, and the preview is included.
An upstream 403 on a write: dispatched, with the receipt (nothing was created) and the role the account lacks in details.required (the eval's T10 probe loop).
An upstream 403 on a read: not_started (nothing was changed), http_status and the role the account lacks in details.required; no details.scope, because the scope was not what refused.
An upstream 409 on a write is E_CONFLICT upstream_conflict: dispatched, with the receipt (nothing merged); receipt rule 4 gives the apply step's cause code.
A batch dry-run: every target once, in order, each with its own op_ id, under one opb_ batch id and one token.
A batch where every item succeeded is ok true with per-item receipts and a summary that matches the items.
A batch with a failed item is ok false: E_PARTIAL because other items applied (partial batches fail).
Any unknown item makes the batch E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, before E_PARTIAL.
Succeeded items may be compact: target, operation id, ok and the result, without the receipt that operation show returns.
A batch error that would break the 2000-character budget keeps both refused items first, then a few successes; omitted counts the rest and summary counts all 30.
The refusal of a 26-issue batch fits the error budget: its preview keeps the first 3 targets and items and says omitted 23; inputs and the token still cover all 26.
operation show returns the record with its preview and receipt; the envelope validates it as an operation.
A partial update is never ok: E_PARTIAL with the staged failure details and the command that finishes the Skill sync.
A signature failure is E_INTEGRITY (not retryable) at a verify stage with the old binary in place.
The full reference as reference prints it: over 8000 characters, and exempt from the success budget (contract.json size_budgets.exempt).
One NDJSON line of pipeline logs --follow: a full envelope plus type item.
The last NDJSON line has type summary.
The error object on its own: exact keys, the core retryable value, conflict token_expired.
A single-target preview: target, changes, bound inputs (snake_case names), the base version re-read at confirm.
A batch preview: targets, total and one item per target with its own op_ id under the opb_ batch id.
A deliver preview is dangerous and names its destinations for the scope check.
An artifact preview names the local path it creates; a file input is bound as {sha256, bytes}, never by path.
A verified delete: the read-back shows the branch is gone.
A local artifact: persistence saved and read back; change and delivery are not_applicable.
A delivery the destination accepted.
An applied record with the preview it was planned from and its receipt.
A dry-run record, written before anything is sent; nothing dispatched yet.
A dispatching record past its lease reads unknown: it blocks new writes to acme/web!5 until resolved.
operation resolve recorded the outcome and its evidence; the target is unblocked.
A batch record lists its items in plan order, each its own operation; the batch status follows from them.
A batch record whose preview is shortened (3 of 12 targets, omitted 9) to fit operation show's budget; the record still lists all 12 items.

A batch too large for operation show's budget lists the items that need attention first, then the done ones, and items_omitted counts the rest (listed + omitted = the preview's total); operation list --batch pages through all of them.
A batch record that cannot be read: its items are unknown, so items is null, the outcome is unknown and the record blocks writes until it is resolved.
An unreadable batch record after operation resolve: the item list is still lost (items null), and the resolution records what the upstream shows.
An item whose own record cannot be read has a null target and status unknown; the batch status follows from the readable items (applied, applied, not_applied: partial).
The blueprint's scope file: change on everything under acme/ and exactly legacy/payments for a week, at most 100 writes.
A dangerous grant without expiry: any merge request of acme/web (key ends in !), one hook, job artifacts into one folder.
An offset page: the offset echoed, the explicit next_offset to pass next and the upstream's total, so a count question needs no paging.
The members incident made honest: an empty list that says it covers direct members only.
A capped in-tool scan says so: truncated with its reason, has_more true and why it cannot continue by cursor.
A dangerous batch stops at the first failure (continue-on-error false): the rest are skipped and counted as skipped.
A full reference generated from the registry: typed params, effects, maturity with evidence references (simulated:, live:, eval:), schemas, the core error table.
reference --index: one compact entry per command, well within 8000 characters.
The grouped index a larger tool returns instead; root-level commands appear as one-command entries.
reference --command "mr update": the entry, its output schema and its error codes, within 4000 characters.
context from local reads: redacted identity, credential source, the state store's protection and the scope in force.
A tool with settings reports the profile in force, where the choice came from (here <PREFIX>_PROFILE), every profile the settings file defines and the file read.
No scope file: reads work, writes will be refused; nothing is granted.
A Windows state directory outside the user profile with no verified ACL reports windows-unverified (doctor warns about it).
A scope whose limits.max_operations is used up: authorization status budget_spent, still naming the scope.
doctor with the five required checks and one tool-specific check; fix is null exactly when a check passes.
changelog --since 1.2.17: entries strictly newer than since, newest first, in Keep a Changelog categories.
A package-manager update: argv built without a shell, signature_status honestly not_checked, Skills synced.
A binary update: the signature was verified in process before the swap.
update is idempotent: already current is a no-op that ran no package manager.
update --check reports a newer version and changes nothing.
An update notice crossing a major version is a warning.
Other notice types carry type, severity and message and may add their own keys.
A success envelope has exactly ok, schema_version, data and meta; request_id at the top level is not allowed.
A failure envelope has exactly ok, schema_version, error and meta; it never carries data.
schema_version is "2.0" in every 2.0 envelope; a 1.x value means the old contract.
meta holds duration_ms, notices and untrusted only.
meta.duration_ms is always present.
A notice's severity is info or warning; failures are errors, not notices.
meta.untrusted paths start at the envelope root (data. or error.details.); items[].title is relative.
data.items is an array, so the path must step into it with []: data.items[].title.
error.message is always the tool's own sentence; upstream text belongs in error.details, so error.message can never be untrusted.
Times are ISO 8601 UTC with Z; an offset time is not.
IDs are strings, even when they look like numbers.
Keys are lowercase snake_case; webUrl is camelCase.
A default success response stays within 8000 characters; a 40-item list with every field belongs on --output or behind --limit and default fields.
Every error's details carry dispatch_state.
Every error's details carry next_action.
E_NOT_FOUND is not retryable; code and retryable follow contract.json error_codes.core exactly.
Error codes are E_ plus upper-case snake case.
E_USAGE names its problem.
problem is one of the contract's values; bad_flag is not (unknown_flag is).
unknown_flag is about one input, so details.parameter names it.
A usage error is found before anything is sent: dispatch_state is not_started.
E_NETWORK is retryable because nothing was sent; after a possible send the code is E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is never retryable: the change may already have happened.
E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN says how to look the operation up.
An unknown outcome means the request may have been sent; dispatch_state cannot be not_started.
lookup is the command that looks up details.operation_id, not another operation.
The refusal of a write without --dry-run or --confirm carries the preview, so the agent can confirm directly.
token_mismatch names the first differing parameter.
unresolved_operation names the operation that blocks the target.
conflict is one of the contract's subtypes; stale_token is not.
An upstream 409 is upstream_conflict; state_drift is the gate's own finding before anything is sent, so it is never dispatched.
A local scope refusal (not_started, no upstream status, no required role) carries details.scope: why, which file, what to grant.
A read that gets a 404 is not_started; dispatched means a write's request reached the upstream, and then the error carries the receipt.
details.scope names the scope file path the person must create or fix.
details.scope.status is missing, invalid, expired, revoked, insufficient or budget_spent.
grant_example is a scope file the person can save after adjusting it; it is valid against the scope schema (here it lacks expires_at).
E_AMBIGUOUS lists at least two candidates; one match is not ambiguous.
E_HUMAN_REQUIRED says what to run once the person has acted.
details.action is one of the contract's human actions.
E_PARTIAL carries the receipt (single write) or items and summary (batch); without them the agent cannot tell what took effect.
E_VERIFY_FAILED carries the receipt whose read-back disagrees.
Batch items in error.details come with their summary.
retry_after_ms is a wait in milliseconds, never negative.
An error envelope stays within 2000 characters; a whole upstream HTML page does not belong in details.
A confirm token has exactly one encoding, ct2_<id part>_<32 hex>; a v1-style ct_ token is rejected.
A re-encoded (upper-case) token is not the canonical token; accepting it would let a used token replay (G05).
A dry-run returns preview, confirm_token, expires_at and operation_id.
Dry-run data has exactly preview, confirm_token, expires_at and operation_id.
A preview that cannot be applied gets no token: confirm_token is null.
The token carries the id part of the operation it was minted for; this one belongs to another operation.
A receipt with an unknown change is E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN by receipt rule 1; reporting it as ok is a false success.
A partial change is E_PARTIAL by receipt rule 2; partial never rounds up to success.
An applied change whose read-back disagrees is E_VERIFY_FAILED (rule 7), not a retryable E_SERVER that invites a second write.
Base profile: change applied with verification not_run is ok (rule 9); E_VERIFY_INCOMPLETE for not_run is the driver profile.
A rolled-back change left nothing applied: receipt rule 5 makes the write ok false with the cause code; ok true is a false success.
data.operation_id names the operation its receipt reports.
Partial batches are ok false (E_PARTIAL); v1's ok true with a failed item is gone.
Any item with an unknown outcome makes the batch E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, even when another item applied.
A batch whose items all succeeded is ok true; E_PARTIAL needs a failed, unknown or skipped item.
Once the binary is replaced the agent gets the command that finishes the Skill sync.
An integrity failure keeps v1's staged failure contract: the stage that failed is named.
Each NDJSON line carries type item or summary.
The error object has exactly code, message, retryable and details; hints go in details.next_action.
can_apply false needs at least one blocked_by entry saying why.
A preview is for a write: its effects include something other than observe.
deliver makes a command dangerous.
A deliver preview names its destinations, so the scope check and the reader see where content goes.
A single-target preview runs under an op_ id; opb_ ids are for batches.
A file input is bound by the digest of its content, {sha256, bytes}; a path is not part of it.
total counts every target: with 3 targets listed and no omitted, total is 3; a preview that leaves targets out says how many in omitted.
Every batch item runs under its own operation id.
A failed execution names the stage that failed.
Outcome dimensions use the contract's values; done is not one.
delivery is not_applicable unless deliver is a declared effect.
A failed read-back names the fields that disagree.
A receipt reports what was observed.
Every mismatched field is reported with the value read back.
A planned operation has not been sent; dispatched_at is null.
resolved records the outcome and evidence operation resolve was given.
status is one of the contract's effective statuses; succeeded is not one.
applied cannot hold a receipt whose outcome is unknown; that operation is unknown until resolved.
A confirm token expires within 15 minutes (contract max_ttl_seconds 900) of the dry-run.
A batch with an item that was not applied is partial, not applied.
A shortened batch lists the items that need attention before the done ones; an applied item first hides the failure the agent came for.
Listed items plus items_omitted must equal the preview's total: 2 + 1 is not 4.
items_omitted belongs to a shortened batch record; a single record has no items to leave out.
A batch record with null items is one that could not be read; nothing in it can show the operation is still running, so its status is unknown (or resolved, once someone records the outcome).
An item with a null target is one whose record cannot be read; its outcome cannot be known, so its status is unknown, not applied.
Scope files are parsed strictly: a duplicate key could hide a wider grant behind a narrow one.
Unknown keys make a scope file invalid; approval is not a scope field.
expires_at is required; null states that the grant does not expire.
A target selector matches subtree or exact.
granted_at is ISO 8601 UTC with Z.
A scope expires after it was granted.
outputs and roots are absolute directories; a relative path depends on the working directory.
limits.max_operations is at least 1.
has_more true needs a way to continue (next_cursor or next_offset) or a continuation_reason.
Exactly one continuation: next_cursor and next_offset together are ambiguous.
A complete list (has_more false) has no continuation.
Every list says whether there is more: the members incident returned items without completeness.
count is the number of items returned, not a total the agent might misread.
A truncated list says why.
A list the tool cut short cannot claim has_more false.
next_offset moves past the items returned; repeating offset re-reads the same page.
On the last page (has_more false) the list ends at offset + count; a larger total contradicts it.
Summary counts equal the item tally: the two skipped items are counted as skipped, not failed.
Batch targets are de-duplicated before execution.
A succeeded item carries no error.
summary has total, succeeded, failed, unknown and skipped.
A shortened list keeps every item with ok false before it lists any success; this one leaves out a refused branch but lists three deleted ones.
A path is a group or a command, never both: mr cannot be a command while mr list exists.
A write command's examples show the --dry-run and --confirm pair.
A dangerous command's examples carry --dangerous.
update is one command outside the confirm gate; it never takes --confirm.
No parameter shadows a global flag; a command-level --format would.
A required parameter has no default.
A secret parameter is never echoed, so it has no default.
Parameter types are string, path, integer, number, boolean, json or enum.
A command binds at most one positional argument to a declared flag.
Core codes keep their contract exit: E_NOT_FOUND exits 3.
Exit 9 is reserved for human-action codes.
The tool's risk tier is at least what its effects need: deliver and configure need T2.
A command's output names an entry of the schema catalog.
verified and stable commands cite their evidence.
A command that declares change is a write; type read with effects change is a contradiction.
deliver makes a command dangerous.
The library built-ins are part of every tree; operation resolve is missing.
An index over 8000 characters returns groups instead (reference --index <group> then lists one group).
An index entry is exactly path, type, effects, dangerous, maturity, summary; params belong to reference --command.
An index is either commands or groups.
Command paths are unique.
reference --command stays within 4000 characters.
error_codes holds exactly the codes the command lists; E_PARTIAL is listed but not described.
schemas holds only the command's output schema.
context reports the scope in force.
A granted scope is named.
state.protection is posix-0700, windows-profile-acl, windows-explicit-acl or windows-unverified.
source none means no profile applies, so the profile cannot have a name.
A usable state store says how it is protected; protection is null only when the store is unavailable.
The state directory is reported as an absolute path.
budget_spent (like expired and revoked) means the scope file was read, so the scope is named.
doctor includes credentials, connectivity, state_store, authorization and version.
A failing check gives its fix.
Check names are unique.
Entries are newest first.
--since returns only versions strictly newer than since.
Changes use the Keep a Changelog categories.
Versions are strict semver; 1.0.12&calc is the payload that reached cmd.exe through npm in the fleet audit.
A partial update is never ok; it is E_PARTIAL with the staged failure details.
On the binary path the signature is verified in process before the swap; not_checked is not acceptable there.
signature_verified is true only when signature_status is verified; package-manager paths report not_checked honestly.
An updated result reports the final state: current_version equals target_version.
An update_available notice names current_version, latest_version, command and checked_at.
An update_available notice has exactly the contract's keys.
An update that crosses a major version is a warning.
